1961 Chrysler Newport Wagon Has Massive V8 Under the Hood To Prove Old-School Is Still Cool
38 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
This 1961 Chrysler Newport Wagon came to life as an entry-level premium family hauler, but it left stock days far behind. The wagon has undergone a heart transplant, transforming it into a hot power wagon that proves that old-school is still cool, no matter the body style.
Back in 1961, the Newport was reintroduced as Chrysler’s low-priced full-size model lineup. It dropped as a major success. Undercutting the flagship New Yorker by nearly $2,000, the Newport helped the brand financially with its base models. 1961 also marked the final year for Chrysler’s large rear tailfins, which this car proudly retains
This build, however, spins around the engine bay. That is where the magic hides. Out went the original factory 361-cubic-inch Firebolt V8 with 265 horsepower, and in went the TNT-style 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) Mopar big-block V8 engine for an explosive kind of road behavior.
However, the listing fails to disclose how much the massive power plant makes under the hood of the Chrysler Newport Wagon right now. Depending on the exact donor year and configuration, a vintage Mopar 440 big-block with a four-barrel carburetor traditionally produced between 350 and 375 gross horsepower from the factory.
Photo: Bring a Trailer With only minor modern upgrades, like aftermarket ignition or intake components, a big-block 440-cubic-inch V8 easily pushes 400 to 500 horsepower. The listing does mention a minor issue where the engine bogs slightly under hard acceleration at times, signaling that the fuel or the ignition timing might require some fine-tuning by its next owner.
What we do know is that an aftermarket oil pressure gauge was mounted directly to the engine firewall. The monstrous power plant throws power to the ground through the rear wheels with the help of a period-correct TorqueFlite three-speed automatic transmission. The driver operates it via the push-button gear selector, built right into the left side of the dashboard panel.
The 1961 Chrysler Newport mirrors Virgil Exner's vision The 1961 Chrysler Newport represents the ultimate peak of Chrysler's space-age Forward Look design era, orchestrated by design guru Virgil Exner. The boldly-styled model that you are looking at is a rare Town & Country hardtop wagon.
This means that it features a continuous open cabin layout with no fixed B-pillar between the front and rear doors. When all side windows are down, the layout creates a sleek, uninterrupted silhouette. When the doors open, those getting on board have unrestricted access.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Up front, the Newport features the iconic angled quad headlights , flanking an aggressively styled, inverse-trapezoidal grille. The striking two-tone Teal Blue and White paint frames the radical, razor-sharp finned rear quarter panels. The wagon rolls on 15-inch chrome wire wheels wrapped in General Ameritrac SE white-stripe tires.
The cabin looks like an incredibly detailed mix of vintage 1960s design and modern luxury. Full-width benches are covered in custom plush parchment leather with pleated inserts. The driver sits in front of Chrysler’s three-dimensional AstraDome control pod.
The futuristic, standalone dome houses a sweep speedometer scaled up to 120 mph (193 kph), sitting alongside gauges that track the fuel level, amperage, coolant temperature, and oil pressure. A remote mirror control and an analog clock are also on board. The car is equipped with air conditioning. The belts, compressor, and pulleys are intact, but the lines and under-dash unit have gone missing.
No garage queen here The five-digit odometer reads nearly 97,000 miles, which means it hasn't spent its entire life locked away in a garage. The one trying to sell the Chrysler Newport Wagon has only driven it 50 miles before he parked it indefinitely. That explains why he is trying to get rid of it now. However, he might have started on the wrong foot by setting a reserve that is too high.
Photo: Bring a Trailer The trunk hosts a stowable, rear-facing third-row bench seat that folds entirely flat into the floor to open up a massive cargo space. To get into those seats, you roll down the power-operated rear window and lower the bottom tailgate.
Instead of the all-drum setup, upgraded power-assisted disc brakes up front and the traditional drums out back provide the stopping power. The car rolled off the production line with power steering back in 1961.
Fast forward to 2026, and the 1961 Chrysler Newport Wagon was auctioned off on Bring a Trailer, but bidding stopped at $28,250, which was under the undisclosed reserve. So the owner is currently stuck with the wagon. The car has been under his ownership for the past five years. He bought it on the same platform back in 2021, after it had reportedly spent 25 years with one family.
It was that family that changed its original white paint to the teal blue and white combination during restoration. Offered with a clean Washington title, it does, however, have some flaws after so many years on the road. The listing notes touch-up paint on the passenger quarter panel, rust repair on the tailgate, and lifting paint on the grille.
Well, maybe the owner will get better luck next time...
